questions.question: In the year of the coronation of Akbar, who among the following was designated as the Wakil of the Mughal kingdom with the title of 'Khan-i-Khanan'?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bairam Khan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Bairam Khan** was a trusted military commander and political advisor of Akbar, the third Mughal emperor of India.
 
• He was appointed as the **Wakil (Prime Minister)** of the Mughal Empire and given the title of **Khan-i-Khanan**, which means "Lord of Lords."
 
• During Akbar’s coronation in 1556, Bairam Khan played a key role in consolidating the Mughal rule and acted as the regent for the young emperor, who was only 13 years old at the time.
 
• Bairam Khan was instrumental in securing Akbar's throne by leading the Mughal forces to victory in the **Second Battle of Panipat (1556)** against Hemu, a powerful rival.
 
• As Wakil and Khan-i-Khanan, Bairam Khan managed the administrative and military affairs of the Mughal Empire during Akbar's early reign, ensuring stability and expansion.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Khan-i-Khanan:**

 
 
• The title "Khan-i-Khanan" was one of the highest titles in the Mughal hierarchy, signifying supreme authority under the emperor.
 
• It was often bestowed upon individuals who demonstrated exceptional loyalty and administrative or military capabilities.
 
 
 
• **Bairam Khan’s Role in the Second Battle of Panipat (1556):**
 
 
• The Second Battle of Panipat was a decisive battle fought between the Mughal forces led by Bairam Khan and the army of Hemu, a Hindu general of the Sur Dynasty.
 
• Hemu was defeated, and this victory ensured the re-establishment of Mughal dominance in northern India.
 
 
 
• **Akbar’s Coronation:**
 
 
• Akbar was crowned as the Mughal emperor in 1556 at Kalanaur, Punjab, following the death of his father, Humayun.
 
• Since Akbar was a minor, Bairam Khan served as his regent, exercising significant authority on his behalf.
 
 
 
• **Bairam Khan’s Downfall:**
 
 
• In 1560, Akbar began asserting his independence and dismissed Bairam Khan from regency.
 
• Bairam Khan was later assassinated in Gujarat while traveling to Mecca for pilgrimage.

questions.question: Foods containing fats and carbohydrates are also called ____________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**energy giving foods**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Foods containing fats and carbohydrates are classified as **energy giving foods** because they provide the body with energy needed for daily activities.
 
• Carbohydrates are the **primary source of energy**, easily broken down into glucose, which fuels the body’s cells.
 
• Fats serve as a **concentrated energy reserve**, providing more than double the energy per gram compared to carbohydrates or proteins.
 
• Examples of energy giving foods include **bread, rice, potatoes (carbohydrates)**, and butter, nuts, and oils (fats).
 
• These foods are essential for maintaining the body’s metabolic functions, especially during physical exertion or intense activities.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Carbohydrates:**

 
 
• Classified as simple (e.g., glucose, fructose) or complex (e.g., starch, fiber).
 
• Provide 4 calories per gram and are the body’s preferred energy source.
 
• Excess carbohydrates are stored as glycogen in the liver and muscles or converted to fat.
 
 
 
• **Fats:**
 
 
• Provide 9 calories per gram, making them the most calorie-dense nutrient.
 
• Include saturated fats (e.g., butter, lard) and unsaturated fats (e.g., olive oil, fish oil).
 
• Essential for absorption of fat-soluble vitamins (A, D, E, and K).
 
 
 
• **Energy Balance:**
 
 
• Maintaining energy balance is crucial for weight management and overall health.
 
• Excess energy intake leads to weight gain, while insufficient intake causes weight loss.
 
 
 
• **Other Energy Sources:**
 
 
• Proteins can also be used for energy, but primarily serve as building blocks for growth and repair.
 
• In cases of prolonged starvation, the body uses fats and proteins for energy.

questions.question: Which of the following is a precious mineral?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Platinum**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Platinum** is one of the most precious and rare minerals found on Earth.
 
• It is highly valued for its **scarcity, durability, and resistance to corrosion**, making it a preferred choice for jewelry and industrial applications.
 
• It is classified as a **noble metal** due to its excellent resistance to chemical reactions.
 
• Platinum is also extensively used in **automobile catalytic converters** to reduce harmful emissions and in various electronic and medical applications.
 
• Its rarity and high demand contribute to its significant economic value.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Hematite**

 
 
• Hematite is an iron oxide mineral primarily used as an ore of iron.
 
• It is not considered a precious mineral but is important in steel manufacturing.
 
 
 
• **Mica**
 
 
• Mica is a group of silicate minerals with properties like elasticity and heat resistance.
 
• It is extensively used in electrical and electronic industries but is not classified as a precious mineral.
 
 
 
• **Bauxite**
 
 
• Bauxite is the primary ore of aluminum and is widely used in aluminum production.
 
• It is not a precious mineral but is crucial in industrial applications.
 
 
 
• **Precious Minerals**
 
 
• Precious minerals like platinum, gold, and diamonds are rare and have high economic and aesthetic value.
 
• They are often used in jewelry, industrial applications, and as investments.

questions.question: The Betul, Hoshangabad and Chhindwara districts of Madhya Pradesh is a part of which of the following Biosphere Reserves?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Pachmarhi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Pachmarhi Biosphere Reserve is located in Madhya Pradesh and includes Betul, Hoshangabad, and Chhindwara districts.
 
• It was established in **1999** by the Government of India to conserve biodiversity and promote sustainable development.
 
• The Pachmarhi Biosphere Reserve is a part of the Satpura range, which is known for its unique flora and fauna.
 
• This reserve is home to several endangered species, including the Indian giant squirrel and flying squirrel.
 
• Pachmarhi Biosphere Reserve is also recognized under the UNESCO Man and Biosphere (MAB) Programme.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Biosphere Reserves in India:**

 
 
• Biosphere reserves are specially designated areas for the conservation of biodiversity, research, and sustainable development.
 
• India has **18 Biosphere Reserves**, including Nilgiri, Sundarbans, Gulf of Mannar, and Nanda Devi.
 
• Ten of these reserves are part of UNESCO’s World Network of Biosphere Reserves.
 
 
 
• **UNESCO Man and Biosphere Programme:**
 
 
• It is an intergovernmental scientific program launched in 1971 to improve the relationship between people and their environment.
 
• The program emphasizes sustainable development, conservation of biodiversity, and scientific research.
 
 
 
• **Satpura Range:**
 
 
• The Satpura range is a prominent mountain range in central India, spanning Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, and Chhattisgarh.
 
• It is rich in biodiversity, containing several forests, wildlife sanctuaries, and national parks.
 
 
 
• **Endangered Species in Pachmarhi Biosphere Reserve:**
 
 
• The reserve is home to endangered species like the Indian giant squirrel, leopard, and Indian pangolin.
 
• Efforts are made to protect these species and their habitats through conservation programs.

questions.question: Which of the following is the oldest dated forts in India, as first mentioned in Alexander the Great's war records, bringing it to the 4th century BCE?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kangra Fort**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Kangra Fort** is considered one of the oldest forts in India, with its origins dating back to the **4th century BCE**.
 
• The fort was mentioned in the war records of **Alexander the Great**, indicating its historical significance during his invasion of India.
 
• Located in **Kangra, Himachal Pradesh**, the fort stands as an emblem of the **Trigarta Kingdom**, which was one of the oldest kingdoms in India.
 
• The fort has witnessed numerous invasions, including attacks by **Mahmud of Ghazni** in the 11th century and **Feroz Shah Tughlaq** in the 14th century.
 
• Its strategic location near the confluence of the **Banganga and Manjhi Rivers** made it a critical stronghold in ancient and medieval India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Trigarta Kingdom:**

 
 
• An ancient kingdom mentioned in the Mahabharata, it was known for its warrior clans and strategic location in the Himalayan region.
 
• The Kangra Fort was the capital of this kingdom, serving as a vital center of power.
 
 
 
• **Alexander’s Invasion of India:**
 
 
• Alexander the Great invaded India in 326 BCE, and his records provide valuable historical insights into the Indian subcontinent during that era.
 
• The mention of Kangra Fort in his war records highlights its prominence even during ancient times.
 
 
 
• **Architecture of Kangra Fort:**
 
 
• The fort is renowned for its massive stone walls and intricate gateways, showcasing ancient Indian military architecture.
 
• It houses temples and palaces, including the **Ambika Devi Temple**, reflecting its cultural and religious significance.
 
 
 
• **Other Ancient Forts in India:**
 
 
• **Gwalior Fort:** Known for its historical importance and architectural brilliance, but built later around the 6th century CE.
 
• **Kumbhalgarh Fort:** Constructed in the 15th century by Rana Kumbha in Rajasthan, famous for its massive walls.
 
• **Mehrangarh Fort:** Built in 1459 by Rao Jodha in Jodhpur, Rajasthan, it is one of the largest forts in India.

questions.question: The Kalidas Samman award is presented by which of the following governments?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Madhya Pradesh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **Kalidas Samman** is a prestigious award presented by the government of Madhya Pradesh to honor excellence in the fields of arts, music, theatre, and literature.
 
• It was established in **1980-81** by the **Madhya Pradesh Department of Culture**.
 
• The award is named after the renowned Sanskrit poet and dramatist **Kalidasa**, widely regarded as one of the greatest classical Sanskrit writers.
 
• The recipients of the award receive a cash prize, a citation, and a shawl as part of the honor.
 
• This award is presented annually and recognizes individuals who have made significant contributions to their respective fields on both national and international levels.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Kalidasa**

 
 
• Kalidasa was an ancient Indian poet and playwright, known for his works in **Sanskrit literature**.
 
• His famous works include **Abhijnanashakuntalam** (a play), **Meghaduta** (a lyrical poem), and **Kumarasambhava** (an epic poem).
 
• He is often considered the **Shakespeare of India** due to his profound impact on Indian classical literature.
 
 
 
• **Other Prestigious Awards by Madhya Pradesh Government**
 
 
• **Tansen Samman**: Awarded for excellence in the field of Hindustani classical music.
 
• **Iqbal Samman**: Given for contributions to Urdu literature and poetry.
 
• **Shikhar Samman**: Recognizes lifetime achievements in various fields of art and culture.
 
 
 
• **Other Indian State Cultural Awards**
 
 
• **Rabindra Puraskar** (West Bengal): Awarded for contributions in literature.
 
• **Kabir Samman** (Madhya Pradesh): Honors contributions to poetry and literature.
 
• **Kerala State Film Awards** (Kerala): Recognizes excellence in the film industry.
 
 
 
• The Kalidas Samman has been awarded to notable figures including **Pt. Ravi Shankar**, **Habib Tanvir**, and **Girish Karnad** for their contributions to the arts.

questions.question: In November 2023, who was appointed as the President-elect of the Federation of Indian Chambers of Commerce and Industry (FICCI)?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Anish Shah**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• In November 2023, **Anish Shah** was appointed as the President-elect of the Federation of Indian Chambers of Commerce and Industry (FICCI).
 
• Anish Shah is the **Managing Director and CEO of the Mahindra Group**, one of India's leading multinational companies.
 
• He will officially take charge as the President of FICCI during its 96th Annual General Meeting in December 2023.
 
• Shah succeeds **Subhrakant Panda**, who served as the FICCI President for the 2022-2023 term.
 
• FICCI is one of India’s oldest and most prominent business organizations, established in 1927, representing various industries across the country.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Federation of Indian Chambers of Commerce and Industry (FICCI):**

 
 
• Established in 1927, FICCI is a non-government, non-profit organization representing India's business and industry interests.
 
• It acts as a bridge between the government and businesses, addressing policy and regulatory issues affecting the economy.
 
• FICCI's activities include policy advocacy, business promotion, and fostering global partnerships.
 
 
 
• **Anish Shah’s Leadership:**
 
 
• Anish Shah is the first professional CEO in the history of the Mahindra Group to oversee all aspects of its operations and strategy.
 
• He has played a pivotal role in driving sustainability and digital transformation within the Mahindra Group.
 
 
 
• **FICCI’s Role in India:**
 
 
• FICCI works closely with the government to shape economic policies and address challenges faced by the business community.
 
• The organization hosts global events such as the India Economic Summit, attracting policymakers and business leaders worldwide.
 
 
 
• **Mahindra Group:**
 
 
• Founded in 1945, Mahindra is a multinational conglomerate headquartered in Mumbai, India.
 
• It operates in sectors like automotive, agriculture, IT, real estate, and finance, with a presence in over 100 countries.

questions.question: Which of the following programmes is taken up by the Government of India for improvement of female literacy rates in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Beti Bachao, Beti Padhao**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Beti Bachao, Beti Padhao (BBBP)** is a flagship program launched by the Government of India on **22 January 2015** at Panipat, Haryana.
 
• It aims to address gender discrimination and improve the declining **Child Sex Ratio (CSR)**, while also promoting education for girls.
 
• The program operates under the joint initiative of the **Ministry of Women and Child Development, Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, and Ministry of Education.**
 
• BBBP implements strategies focusing on **advocacy, community participation, and local-level interventions** to eliminate gender bias.
 
• The scheme has been instrumental in raising awareness about the importance of **female literacy, gender equality, and empowering girls** through education and social change.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Child Sex Ratio (CSR):**

 
 
• CSR refers to the number of girls per 1,000 boys in the age group of 0-6 years.
 
• India recorded a declining CSR over the years due to practices like female infanticide and prenatal sex determination.
 
• BBBP aims to reverse this trend through awareness campaigns and legal enforcement.
 
 
 
• **Components of BBBP:**
 
 
• **Advocacy campaigns** to promote awareness about gender equality and female education.
 
• **Multi-sectoral action:** Implementation at district levels through effective coordination among government departments.
 
• **Monitoring mechanisms:** Regular tracking of CSR and education-related indicators in targeted districts.
 
 
 
• **Government Interventions for Female Education:**
 
 
• Programs like **Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan** aim to provide universal access to elementary education.
 
• **Kasturba Gandhi Balika Vidyalaya** focuses on improving access to education for girls from disadvantaged communities.
 
 
 
• **Legal Framework Supporting BBBP:**
 
 
• The **Pre-Conception and Pre-Natal Diagnostic Techniques (PCPNDT) Act, 1994**, prohibits sex-selective abortions.
 
• Government policies are also aligned with the **Right to Education Act, 2009**, ensuring free and compulsory education for children aged 6-14 years.

questions.question: As per the National Multidimensional Poverty Index 2021, which of the following groups of states is the poorest?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bihar, Uttar Pradesh, Jharkhand**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• As per the **National Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI) 2021**, Bihar, Uttar Pradesh, and Jharkhand are among the poorest states in India.
 
• Bihar has the highest poverty rate in the country, with **51.91%** of its population classified as multidimensionally poor.
 
• Jharkhand follows Bihar with **42.16%** of its population living in multidimensional poverty.
 
• Uttar Pradesh is also among the poorest states, with **37.79%** of its population falling under the poverty index.
 
• The MPI measures poverty through three dimensions: **health, education, and standard of living**, encompassing 12 indicators.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **National Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI):**

 
 
• It is developed by NITI Aayog in collaboration with the **Oxford Poverty and Human Development Initiative (OPHI)** and the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP).
 
• The MPI uses the **Global Multidimensional Poverty Index methodology** to assess poverty at the national level.
 
• The index includes three dimensions: **health, education, and standard of living**, with 12 indicators such as nutrition, child mortality, years of schooling, and access to cooking fuel, sanitation, and electricity.
 
 
 
• **Global Context:**
 
 
• The Global Multidimensional Poverty Index is published annually by OPHI and UNDP.
 
• India's performance in the global MPI influences its national policies and poverty alleviation programs.
 
 
 
• **Poverty Alleviation Programs in India:**
 
 
• Programs like the **Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana**, **National Rural Employment Guarantee Scheme** (MGNREGA), and **National Food Security Act** aim to reduce poverty in the country.
 
• These programs focus on providing housing, employment, and food security to the poorest sections of society.
 
 
 
• **Regional Disparities:**
 
 
• States like Bihar, Jharkhand, and Uttar Pradesh experience high poverty rates due to factors like **low industrialization, inadequate infrastructure, and poor access to education and healthcare**.
 
• In contrast, states like Kerala and Punjab perform better in the MPI due to higher investments in social welfare and infrastructure.

questions.question: Which folk dance has its roots in Maharashtra?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Lavani**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Lavani** is a traditional folk dance and music form that originated in the state of Maharashtra, India.
 
• It combines **graceful movements**, powerful rhythms, and expressive storytelling, often performed to the beats of the **"Dholki," a percussion instrument.**
 
• This dance form primarily focuses on themes of **romance, social issues, and devotion**, making it culturally significant in Maharashtra.
 
• Lavani is performed by women, traditionally dressed in nine-yard sarees, accompanied by energetic gestures and expressive facial expressions.
 
• The genre gained popularity during the **Peshwa era** and continues to be an important part of Maharashtra's cultural heritage.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Folk Dance Forms Across India:**

 
 
• **Garba and Dandiya** are traditional dance forms from Gujarat, performed during Navratri celebrations.
 
• **Bihu** is a folk dance from Assam, performed during the Bihu festival to celebrate the Assamese New Year.
 
• Other prominent folk dances include **Ghoomar** (Rajasthan), **Bhangra** (Punjab), and **Chhau** (Odisha).
 
 
 
• **Lavani's Cultural Significance:**
 
 
• Lavani has historically been used to convey **social messages** and entertain audiences during wartime.
 
• The performances often highlight women’s **empowerment, emotions, and societal issues**.
 
 
 
• **Types of Lavani:**
 
 
• There are two main types of Lavani: **Nirguni Lavani**, which is devotional, and **Shringari Lavani**, which focuses on romance and sensuality.
 
• Both types are integral to the cultural storytelling tradition of Maharashtra.
 
 
 
• **Performance and Costumes:**
 
 
• Performers wear vibrant nine-yard sarees and adorn themselves with traditional Maharashtrian jewelry.
 
• The dramatic expressions and rhythmic footwork form the essence of Lavani performances.

questions.question: Ravikirti was the court poet of which ruler?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Pulakeshin II**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Ravikirti was the court poet of **Pulakeshin II**, a prominent ruler of the Chalukya dynasty.
 
• He is best known for composing the **Aihole inscription**, which details the achievements of Pulakeshin II.
 
• The Aihole inscription, written in Sanskrit, is inscribed at the Meguti Jain temple in Aihole, Karnataka.
 
• Ravikirti's inscription describes Pulakeshin II's military conquests, including his victory over Harshavardhana and his expansion of the Chalukya empire.
 
• This inscription is considered an important historical source for understanding the Chalukya dynasty and its socio-political context.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Pulakeshin II (610–642 CE):**

 
 
• Pulakeshin II was one of the greatest rulers of the Chalukya dynasty and ruled from Badami in present-day Karnataka.
 
• He successfully resisted the northward expansion of Harshavardhana, as documented in Ravikirti's Aihole inscription.
 
• Under his reign, the Chalukya empire expanded to include large parts of the Deccan Plateau.
 
 
 
• **Aihole:**
 
 
• Aihole is an important historical site known as the "Cradle of Indian Temple Architecture."
 
• It was a major cultural and architectural center during the Chalukya period.
 
 
 
• **Chalukya Dynasty:**
 
 
• The Chalukyas were a prominent South Indian dynasty that ruled from the 6th to the 12th century CE.
 
• They are known for their contributions to art, architecture, and literature, as seen in their temple constructions and inscriptions.
 
 
 
• **Significance of Court Poets:**
 
 
• Court poets like Ravikirti played a crucial role in documenting the achievements of their patrons.
 
• Such inscriptions often combined historical records with poetic flourishes, serving as both propaganda and cultural artifacts.

questions.question: The basic structure of the Indian Constitution stands on the Government of India Act, ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1935**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Government of India Act, 1935, served as the **foundation for the Indian Constitution**, providing many administrative structures and features.
 
• The Act introduced significant elements like the **federal system, provincial autonomy, and bicameralism**, which were later adopted in the Indian Constitution.
 
• The **Indian Constitution** borrowed key features such as the structure of governance, emergency provisions, and the division of powers from this act.
 
• The Act established an **All-India Federation**, although it was never fully implemented as princely states did not join.
 
• The **Government of India Act, 1935**, is considered the longest and most detailed act of British India, influencing the structure of modern Indian governance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Federal Structure:** The Government of India Act, 1935, introduced the concept of a federal structure with powers divided between the Centre and provinces.
 
• **Provincial Autonomy:** The Act granted autonomy to provinces, allowing elected representatives to have more control over local governance.
 
• **Instrument of Instructions:** These were guidelines for the Governor-General and Governors, later incorporated into the Directive Principles of State Policy in the Indian Constitution.
 
• **Bicameralism:** The Act introduced bicameral legislatures at the Centre, a feature retained in the Indian Constitution with the Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha.
 
• **Emergency Provisions:** The Act had provisions for emergency powers, which were later adapted and expanded in the Indian Constitution under Articles 352, 356, and 360.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of anaerobic activity?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Jumping**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Anaerobic activities** are high-intensity, short-duration exercises where the body relies on energy stored in muscles instead of oxygen.
 
• **Jumping** is a classic example of anaerobic activity because it requires quick bursts of energy without sustained oxygen supply.
 
• During jumping, muscles use **stored adenosine triphosphate (ATP)** and glycogen for energy production.
 
• Other examples of anaerobic activities include sprinting, weightlifting, and high-intensity interval training (HIIT).
 
• Anaerobic activities help improve **muscle strength, endurance, and power** while promoting fat loss and increasing metabolic rate.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Aerobic vs Anaerobic Activities:**

 
 
• **Aerobic activities** rely on oxygen for energy and are typically moderate-intensity, long-duration exercises (e.g., walking, swimming).
 
• **Anaerobic activities** are high-intensity, short-duration exercises that do not rely on oxygen (e.g., jumping, sprinting).
 
 
 
• **Energy Systems in Anaerobic Activity:**
 
 
• Anaerobic energy is provided by the **ATP-PC system** (phosphocreatine) and **anaerobic glycolysis**.
 
• These systems supply energy rapidly but for short durations (up to 2 minutes).
 
 
 
• **Benefits of Anaerobic Exercises:**
 
 
• Boosts muscle strength and power.
 
• Improves bone density and joint function.
 
• Increases metabolic rate, aiding in fat loss.
 
 
 
• **Risks and Precautions:**
 
 
• Anaerobic activities can strain muscles and joints if performed without proper warm-up or technique.
 
• Consult a fitness professional and avoid overtraining to prevent injuries.

questions.question:
Select the correct order of processes used for water purification in waterworks.

1. Filtration

2. Chlorination

3. Suspended impurity sedimentation

4. Solid impurity sedimentation
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**4-3-1-2**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The correct sequence for water purification in waterworks is: **solid impurity sedimentation → suspended impurity sedimentation → filtration → chlorination**.
 
• **Solid impurity sedimentation**: Involves allowing larger particles and debris to settle at the bottom of the tank.
 
• **Suspended impurity sedimentation**: Addition of coagulants like alum helps smaller particles clump together and settle.
 
• **Filtration**: Water passes through sand, gravel, and other filter media to remove fine particles and impurities.
 
• **Chlorination**: Disinfection by adding chlorine to eliminate harmful microorganisms and pathogens.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Coagulation and Flocculation**:

 
 
• These are essential processes where chemicals like alum are added to water to aggregate suspended particles into larger flocs.
 
• Flocs settle faster during sedimentation, improving water clarity.
 
 
 
• **Chlorination**:
 
 
• A widely used disinfection technique in water treatment plants.
 
• It effectively kills bacteria, viruses, and other microbes, ensuring safe drinking water.
 
 
 
• **Filtration Media**:
 
 
• Common filtration materials include sand, gravel, and activated carbon.
 
• These materials help in trapping fine particles and adsorbing organic impurities.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Sedimentation**:
 
 
• Reduces the load on downstream filtration systems by removing large and suspended impurities early in the process.
 
• Enhances the efficiency of the entire water purification process.

questions.question: Mysore Brothers are known for playing which musical instrument?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Violin**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Mysore Brothers, Dr. Mysore Manjunath and Dr. Mysore Nagaraj, are renowned for their exceptional artistry on the **violin**.
 
• They are globally acclaimed musicians in the field of **Carnatic classical music**, a prominent form of South Indian classical music.
 
• The brothers have performed in prestigious venues worldwide, including the **Royal Albert Hall in London** and the Sydney Opera House.
 
• They are known for their unique blend of technical brilliance, emotive expressions, and **improvisational skills** in their violin performances.
 
• Dr. Mysore Manjunath and Dr. Mysore Nagaraj have received numerous accolades, including the **Sangeet Natak Akademi Award** and the Karnataka Rajyotsava Award, for their contributions to music.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Violin in Carnatic Music**

 
 
• The violin was introduced into Carnatic music in the 18th century by Baluswami Dikshitar, who adapted it to suit Indian classical music styles.
 
• In Carnatic music, the violin is often used as an accompaniment instrument to vocalists and also as a solo instrument.
 
• Unlike in Western classical music, the violin in Carnatic music is played while sitting cross-legged, with the instrument resting on the player’s shoulder and ankle.
 
 
 
• **Carnatic Music**
 
 
• Carnatic music is one of the two main traditions of Indian classical music, the other being Hindustani music.
 
• It primarily focuses on **kriti compositions**, which are devotional songs composed by revered saints like Tyagaraja, Muthuswami Dikshitar, and Syama Sastri.
 
• Raga (melodic framework) and Tala (rhythmic cycles) form the backbone of Carnatic music.
 
 
 
• **Violin Techniques in Carnatic Music**
 
 
• Carnatic violinists use intricate bowing techniques and microtonal variations (gamakas) to match the expressive requirements of the raga.
 
• The techniques emphasize smooth transitions between notes, creating a continuous and melodic flow.
 
 
 
• **Recognition of Mysore Brothers**
 
 
• The Mysore Brothers have contributed significantly to spreading Indian classical music on global platforms.
 
• Their collaborations with Western classical, jazz, and world music artists have added a unique dimension to their art.

questions.concept: Socio - Religious Reform Movements in the 19th and 20th CE India
questions.question: In which of the places was Arya Samaj founded?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bombay**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Arya Samaj was founded by **Swami Dayanand Saraswati** in 1875 in Bombay.
 
• The main objective of Arya Samaj was to reform Hinduism by promoting **Vedic principles** and opposing superstitions and social evils.
 
• Swami Dayanand Saraswati advocated the philosophy of "**Back to the Vedas**" to revive the spiritual essence of ancient Hindu scriptures.
 
• The Arya Samaj actively worked toward **abolishing caste discrimination** and promoting education, especially for women.
 
• The organization also played a significant role in India's **social and cultural awakening** during the 19th and 20th centuries.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Swami Dayanand Saraswati**

 
 
• Born in 1824, Swami Dayanand was a Hindu spiritual leader and social reformer.
 
• He authored the book "**Satyarth Prakash**" (The Light of Truth), which laid the foundation for Arya Samaj's principles.
 
• He opposed idol worship and rituals that had no basis in the Vedic scriptures.
 
 
 
• **Key Principles of Arya Samaj**
 
 
• Belief in the authority of the Vedas as the ultimate source of knowledge.
 
• Promotion of monotheism and rejection of polytheism and idol worship.
 
• Encouragement of universal education, social equality, and women's empowerment.
 
 
 
• **Educational Contributions**
 
 
• Arya Samaj established schools and colleges, such as the **DAV (Dayanand Anglo Vedic) institutions**, which are renowned for their emphasis on value-based education.
 
• Promoted the teaching of Sanskrit and Vedic literature.
 
 
 
• **Social Reform Activities**
 
 
• Opposition to untouchability and promotion of social equality.
 
• Campaign against child marriage and promotion of widow remarriage.
 
• Arya Samaj played a significant role in India's freedom struggle by fostering national pride and cultural revival.

questions.question: Waiting for a Visa' is the autobiography of:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bhimrao Ambedkar**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **'Waiting for a Visa'** is a short autobiographical account written by Dr. Bhimrao Ambedkar, one of India's foremost social reformers and the chief architect of the Indian Constitution.
 
• The text highlights the discrimination and untouchability faced by Dalits during Dr. Ambedkar's lifetime and serves as a critical document on caste-based inequalities in India.
 
• It is considered one of the most important works in understanding Dr. Ambedkar's early life and experiences as a Dalit in pre-independent India.
 
• The autobiography was used as a teaching text at Columbia University, where Dr. Ambedkar pursued higher education.
 
• 'Waiting for a Visa' is a concise yet impactful account that sheds light on the harsh realities of caste oppression and social injustice.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bhimrao Ambedkar**

 
 
• He was born on April 14, 1891, in Mhow, Madhya Pradesh, into a Dalit family.
 
• Ambedkar was the driving force behind India's Constitution and a staunch advocate for equality and social justice.
 
• He led efforts to abolish untouchability and worked extensively for the upliftment of marginalized communities.
 
• He converted to Buddhism in 1956, along with millions of followers, as part of a movement against caste discrimination.
 
 
 
• **Untouchability**
 
 
• A practice rooted in the caste system, untouchability subjected certain communities to severe discrimination and social exclusion.
 
• Ambedkar fought against these practices and advocated for constitutional safeguards to eliminate caste-based inequalities.
 
• Article 17 of the Indian Constitution abolishes untouchability in all forms.
 
 
 
• **Columbia University**
 
 
• Dr. Ambedkar earned his master's degree and PhD from Columbia University in the United States.
 
• His thesis, “The Problem of the Rupee,” laid the foundation for India's financial policies.
 
 
 
• **Contribution to India's Constitution**
 
 
• Dr. Ambedkar was the chairman of the Drafting Committee of the Indian Constitution.
 
• He introduced several provisions to ensure social justice, such as reservations for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes.
 
• His work on the Constitution emphasized equality, liberty, and fraternity.

questions.question: What is the standard length of a cricket pitch?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**22 yards**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• A cricket pitch is a rectangular area located at the center of the field, measuring precisely **22 yards (20.12 meters) in length and 10 feet (3.05 meters) in width.**
 
• The pitch is used for bowling, batting, and running between the wickets during play.
 
• The length of 22 yards is internationally standardized by the **International Cricket Council (ICC).**
 
• The stumps are set at each end of the pitch, and the popping creases are marked 4 feet in front of the stumps.
 
• The pitch's dimensions have remained consistent since the early development of cricket in England in the 17th century.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Terminology Related to Cricket Pitch:**

 
 
• **Crease:** Lines drawn on the pitch to define areas for the bowler and batsman.
 
• **Wicket:** Consists of three stumps and two bails, placed at each end of the pitch.
 
• **Popping Crease:** The line a batsman must reach to avoid being run out.
 
• **Bowling Crease:** The line where the stumps are placed.
 
 
 
• **Pitch Conditions:**
 
 
• Pitches can vary in nature—**flat pitches favor batsmen**, while grassy or cracked pitches benefit bowlers.
 
• In Test cricket, pitch conditions change significantly over five days, affecting gameplay.
 
 
 
• **Historical Development:**
 
 
• The 22-yard measurement has been in place since cricket's codification in the 18th century.
 
• It was derived from the traditional English unit of measurement called "chain," which equals 22 yards.
 
 
 
• **Role of ICC:**
 
 
• The ICC regulates pitch preparation to ensure consistency and fairness in international matches.
 
• Pitch inspections are conducted to avoid undue advantages for either batsmen or bowlers.

questions.question: Which of the following groups of ports are located on the bank of the Bay of Bengal?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Haldia and Paradip**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Haldia** and **Paradip** ports are located along the eastern coast of India, on the banks of the Bay of Bengal.
 
• **Haldia Port** is situated in West Bengal and serves as a major trade gateway for eastern India.
 
• **Paradip Port** is located in Odisha and is one of the largest ports in India, strategically positioned for handling bulk cargo.
 
• Both ports contribute significantly to India's maritime trade and are vital for the export of goods such as coal, iron ore, and petroleum products.
 
• These ports are known for their role in boosting economic connectivity and industrial development in their respective regions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bay of Bengal**

 
 
• It is the largest bay in the world and is bordered by India, Bangladesh, Myanmar, and Sri Lanka.
 
• The bay is a critical region for international maritime trade, with several major ports located along its coastline.
 
• It connects the Indian Ocean to Southeast Asia through key shipping routes.
 
 
 
• **Major Ports in India**
 
 
• India has 13 major ports, including Paradip, Haldia, Mumbai, Chennai, and Visakhapatnam.
 
• Major ports are managed by the central government and serve as hubs for international trade.
 
• These ports handle a significant portion of India’s cargo traffic, including exports and imports.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Ports**
 
 
• Ports serve as gateways for international trade and contribute to economic growth.
 
• They facilitate the transportation of goods, reduce logistics costs, and enhance connectivity.
 
• Ports play a crucial role in industrial development by supporting supply chain operations.
 
 
 
• **Eastern Coast of India**
 
 
• The eastern coast of India includes states like West Bengal, Odisha, Andhra Pradesh, and Tamil Nadu.
 
• This region is known for its rich biodiversity, extensive coastline, and economic activities.
 
• Ports along the eastern coast are vital for trade with Southeast Asia and East Asia.

questions.question: What is the name of the scheme launched by the Government of India in 2023 to effectively resolve pending contractual disputes?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Vivad se Vishwas II**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The "Vivad se Vishwas II" scheme was launched by the Government of India in 2023 to resolve **long-pending contractual disputes** involving government and public sector enterprises.
 
• The scheme is aimed at **expeditiously settling disputes** to unlock funds stuck in litigation and promote ease of doing business.
 
• It is designed to offer a **voluntary settlement mechanism** to contractors and litigants by providing an opportunity to settle disputes amicably.
 
• The scheme applies to disputes that are **pending as of 30th September 2022**, involving arbitral awards and court orders.
 
• The government expects this initiative to **reduce litigation costs**, free up resources, and strengthen the business environment in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Vivad se Vishwas I**

 
 
• Launched in 2020, this scheme was introduced to resolve **direct tax disputes** and reduce litigation in income tax matters.
 
• It provided taxpayers an opportunity to settle their disputes by paying only the disputed tax amount, with **complete waiver of interest and penalty**.
 
• The scheme helped clear a significant backlog of tax-related cases in various tribunals and courts.
 
 
 
• **Key Objectives of Vivad se Vishwas II**
 
 
• Facilitate faster resolution of disputes to **avoid prolonged litigation**.
 
• Enable contractors to **recover dues** and reinvest in economic activities.
 
• Improve the ease of doing business by building trust between the government and private sector entities.
 
 
 
• **Arbitration in India**
 
 
• Arbitration is a method of resolving disputes outside the judiciary system, typically involving a neutral third party (arbitrator).
 
• The **Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996**, governs the arbitration process in India.
 
• It aims to provide a speedy and cost-effective alternative to traditional court litigation.
 
 
 
• **Ease of Doing Business in India**
 
 
• The Government of India has been actively implementing measures to improve India's rank in the **World Bank's Ease of Doing Business Index**.
 
• Steps include streamlining business registration, resolving insolvency faster, and digitizing compliance processes.
 
• Schemes like "Vivad se Vishwas II" are part of these reforms to create a more investor-friendly environment.

questions.question: Shuddhi movement was initiated by which of the following organisations?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Arya Samaj**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Shuddhi Movement was initiated by **Arya Samaj** in the late 19th and early 20th centuries.
 
• It aimed to reconvert individuals, especially those who had converted to Islam or Christianity, back to Hinduism.
 
• The movement was spearheaded by **Swami Dayanand Saraswati**, the founder of Arya Samaj, and later continued by leaders like **Swami Shraddhanand**.
 
• The Shuddhi Movement was part of Arya Samaj’s broader agenda to reform Hindu society and restore its cultural and religious identity.
 
• The movement also aimed at the abolition of untouchability by embracing lower-caste individuals into the Hindu fold.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Arya Samaj**

 
 
• Founded by **Swami Dayanand Saraswati** in 1875, Arya Samaj is a socio-religious reform movement in India.
 
• It emphasizes the authority of the Vedas and promotes monotheism while rejecting idol worship and rituals.
 
• The movement played a significant role in the spread of education and social reform in India.
 
 
 
• **Swami Shraddhanand**
 
 
• A prominent leader of Arya Samaj, Swami Shraddhanand was instrumental in promoting the Shuddhi Movement.
 
• He was actively involved in the reconversion of Malkana Rajputs and other Hindu groups who had converted to Islam or Christianity.
 
 
 
• **Shuddhi Movement and Social Reform**
 
 
• The movement aimed to unify and strengthen the Hindu community by addressing social divisions.
 
• It worked to assimilate marginalized communities into mainstream Hinduism, including those labeled as "untouchables."
 
 
 
• **Criticism of the Shuddhi Movement**
 
 
• The movement faced criticism for fostering religious conversions and communal tensions.
 
• It was opposed by leaders of other religious communities, including Muslims and Christians, for its reconversion agenda.

questions.question: Which financial products are commonly offered by Microfinance Institutions in India?

options.text: Savings, credit and insurance services tailored for low-income individuals

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Savings, credit and insurance services tailored for low-income individuals**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Microfinance Institutions (MFIs) in India primarily provide **financial products and services** to economically disadvantaged groups, particularly in rural and semi-urban areas.
 
• The main offerings include **savings accounts**, small-value loans (microcredit), and **micro-insurance products** tailored to the needs of low-income individuals.
 
• MFIs often focus on promoting **financial inclusion** by offering these services to populations that lack access to traditional banking systems.
 
• Micro-loans are typically **unsecured** and range from a few thousand rupees to assist individuals in starting or expanding small businesses.
 
• MFIs may also provide financial literacy programs to help beneficiaries better manage their resources and improve their economic stability.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Microcredit:** Small loans provided to individuals or groups without requiring collateral, often used for income-generating activities or small businesses.
 
• **Self-Help Groups (SHGs):** Many MFIs work with SHGs, which are community-based groups that pool savings and access microfinance services collectively.
 
• **Financial Inclusion:** The process of ensuring access to financial services like savings, credit, and insurance to all segments of society, particularly vulnerable and low-income groups.
 
• **Key Players in Indian Microfinance:** Some prominent MFIs in India include SKS Microfinance, Bandhan Bank, Ujjivan Financial Services, and Spandana Sphoorty.
 
• **Regulation of MFIs:** The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) regulates MFIs and has set guidelines for their functioning, including interest rate caps and loan repayment structures.

questions.question: Which edition of the ODI Cricket World Cup was held in India in 2023?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**13th**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The 2023 ICC Men's ODI Cricket World Cup was the **13th edition** of the tournament.
 
• It was hosted solely by **India** for the first time, although India had co-hosted earlier editions in 1987, 1996, and 2011.
 
• The tournament featured a total of **10 teams**, competing in a round-robin format followed by knockouts.
 
• The event was organized by the **International Cricket Council (ICC)**, which is the global governing body for cricket.
 
• India became the first country to host the ODI Cricket World Cup independently, highlighting its growing stature in international cricket.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **ODI Cricket World Cup**

 
 
• The ICC Men's Cricket World Cup is the premier international championship of One Day International (ODI) cricket.
 
• The tournament has been held every four years since its inception in 1975.
 
• Australia is the most successful team, having won the tournament five times.
 
 
 
• **2023 World Cup Format**
 
 
• The tournament followed a round-robin format where all 10 teams played against each other once.
 
• The top four teams advanced to the semi-finals, leading to the final match to determine the champion.
 
 
 
• **Past ODI World Cups in India**
 
 
• India co-hosted the 1987 World Cup with Pakistan, the first time the tournament was held outside England.
 
• India co-hosted again in 1996 with Pakistan and Sri Lanka, and in 2011 with Sri Lanka and Bangladesh.
 
• India won the 2011 edition, defeating Sri Lanka in the final at Wankhede Stadium, Mumbai.
 
 
 
• **Key Players and Teams**
 
 
• Top cricketing nations like India, Australia, England, Pakistan, and New Zealand participated in the 2023 World Cup.
 
• Key players included Virat Kohli (India), Joe Root (England), Babar Azam (Pakistan), and Trent Boult (New Zealand).

questions.question: Which of the following Articles of the Constitution has a provision that 'all executive actions of the Government of India shall be expressed to be taken in the name of the President'?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 77 (1)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Article 77 (1)** of the Indian Constitution mandates that **all executive actions of the Government of India must be expressed to be taken in the name of the President**.
 
• This provision ensures that the President, as the formal head of the executive, is recognized in all governmental actions, even though the real powers are exercised by the Council of Ministers headed by the Prime Minister.
 
• The **President of India** is the nominal executive authority, while the actual execution of policies and decisions lies with the Council of Ministers.
 
• This article is vital for maintaining the parliamentary system of governance, ensuring that all executive actions are performed under a unified authority.
 
• Article 77 further provides guidelines on how orders and instruments made in the President's name are authenticated and ensures their validity in legal proceedings.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 53:** The executive power of the Union is vested in the President and is exercised by him either directly or through officers subordinate to him in accordance with the Constitution.
 
• **Council of Ministers:** Article 74 mandates that the President shall act in accordance with the advice of the Council of Ministers headed by the Prime Minister.
 
• **President's Role:** The President serves as the ceremonial head of the state, while the actual governance is conducted by the Council of Ministers, maintaining the balance of power in a parliamentary system.
 
• **Authentication of Orders:** Article 77 (2) specifies that orders and other instruments made in the President’s name must be authenticated as per the rules framed under this article to ensure their legal validity.
 
• **Article 78:** This article outlines the duties of the Prime Minister, including keeping the President informed of all decisions of the Council of Ministers and matters relating to the administration of the Union.
